Auto-Generate an Importance-Threshold Grid for Random-Forest STABL (Experimental)

auto_rf_threshold_grid.Rd

Builds the random-forest analog of auto_lambda_grid(): one ranger forest with permutation importance is fit on the full data, and the grid is taken from quantiles of the pooled importance distribution (probs = seq(0.5, 0.999, length.out = n_grid)). Experimental extension beyond Python STABL.

Usage

auto_rf_threshold_grid(x, y, n_grid = 30L, num_trees = 500L, seed = NULL)

Arguments

x

A matrix or data.frame of features (samples in rows).

y

Outcome vector.

n_grid

Positive integer; number of grid points.

num_trees

Positive integer; number of trees per ranger forest.

seed

Optional integer seed for the forest fit.

Value

A data.frame with columns lambda (the importance threshold) and threshold (identical), sorted in decreasing order so the path runs sparse-to-dense, matching the lambda-path convention used by stabl_fit().

See also

make_ranger_adapter(), auto_lambda_grid().

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1L)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 6), 60, 6,
              dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:60), paste0("f", 1:6)))
  y <- setNames(x[, 1] * x[, 2] * 0.5 + rnorm(60, sd = 0.3), rownames(x))
  grid <- auto_rf_threshold_grid(x, y, n_grid = 5L, num_trees = 100L, seed = 1L)
  grid
}
#>        lambda   threshold
#> 1 0.056898277 0.056898277
#> 2 0.049516610 0.049516610
#> 3 0.036206947 0.036206947
#> 4 0.014181369 0.014181369
#> 5 0.004090671 0.004090671
